title: Country Turns To Gaming Legend To Counterplay Online Gambling Epidemic
description: Online gambling has been in the news a fair bit recently, with the ease of getting into online sportsbook betting becoming a hotly contested issue in the United States and popular prediction markets being subjected to increased controversy and government scrutiny. It's hardly limited to the United States, however, as illicit online gambling has wide appeal across much of Asia, despite local laws forbidding much of it. South Korea in particular has seen an uptick in online gambling, particularly among youth, many of whom have gone to extreme lengths to obtain money to spend on gambling or cover their debts. To help combat the growing problem, the government has teamed up with one of the most famous figures in global esports, League of Legends prodigy Lee Sang-hyeok, better known by the handle "Faker." As reported by the Seoul Economic Daily, Faker has been made an honorary police officer with the title of Senior Officer. The rationale behind this appointment is that "Lee is an esports player with high recognition at home and abroad and has consistently practiced the values of self-management and restraint throughout his long career, serving as a role model for young people." In this role, Lee will be producing public service announcements, such as videos and posters, to help promote South Korea's Youth Cyber Gambling Voluntary Reporting System, which aims to help youngsters with online gambling problems. As an added incentive to free themselves of gambling addiction, those who join the program may receive Faker's autographed uniform, which the article notes "will be delivered to young people who have overcome gambling addiction by faithfully participating in treatment programs, serving as encouragement for their healthy return to daily life." This honor is hardly the first for Lee, who was the first Korean eSports athlete to receive the Cheongnyong Medal, a top honor for the country's athletes. He's also due to appear on South Korean postage and has recently debuted…

title: Call Of Duty Is Introducing A New “Classic” Matchmaking System In Season 5
description: Season 5 arrives to Black Ops 7 on July 23, and Activision has revealed the season is also being paired with a new multiplayer matchmaking system inspired by the older Call of Duty games. Here we highlight all the modes affected and what you need to know before Season 5 launches. Call of Duty's matchmaking has long been a hot topic of the community, and Black Ops 7 was the first title in years to receive a matchmaking system that didn't heavily favor a skill-based formula. The game currently features "Open" playlists, which Activision previously described as only including "minimal skill consideration," or, in essence, little or no SBMM. This was presumed to be closer to the matchmaking system of the older Call of Duty games. Now, Call of Duty is changing matchmaking again. The publisher describes this new system as being "inspired" by the classic matchmaking of past games. This new matchmaking will be implemented in Black Ops 7's playlists for Black Ops Classic, Quick Play, and Party Games, but the current existing Open playlist will remain. The publisher doesn't explain how these Open and Classic systems are different, but this new formula should still lean away from heavy skill-based matchmaking of recent years. "Over the past year, we've continued to learn a lot about multiplayer matchmaking through player data and community feedback," Activision said in an announcement on social media. "We're also excited to see all the recent love for Black Ops and Black Ops 2, which reinforced that there are many elements of those experiences that players appreciate." The publisher's statement suggests this change could stem from the recent success of the Black Ops 1 and Black Ops 2 ports for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. Activision confirmed that the Modern Warfare 4 beta will feature Open playlist options, which will presumably feel similar to the matchmaking system of Black Ops 7's current Open playlists. However, any success around this new system introduced in Season…

title: Magic: The Gathering’s Multiverse Is Gearing Up For Its Next Big Story In 2027
description: A lot of the mainstream buzz around Magic: The Gathering in recent months has revolved around its Universes Beyond initiative, which has introduced outside IP into the decades-old card game. Final Fantasy, Avatar: The Last Airbender, and most recently Marvel Super Heroes have released full expansions, with The Hobbit and Star Trek set to arrive later this year. However, the reason those outside IP were able to join Magic was because of the strong universe of characters and locations the game has built in those 30-plus years. At MagicCon Amsterdam, the Preview Panel focused on Magic's established multiverse, as the hour-long panel revealed all three in-universe sets coming to Magic in 2027, with the Universes Beyond announcements saved for another day. After the panel, we sat down with many of the key architects of the 2027 slate, both in Q&A roundtables and in one-on-one interviews, to talk about each of the three Magic multiverse worlds players will visit next year. We'll explore an underwater world making its MTG debut, a new twist on an established plane, and a place thought lost in Magic's lore. Under the sea with Nauctis: The Sunken Realm 2027's first Magic: The Gathering expansion will be Nauctis: The Sunken Realm on February 5, which is set in a world that's entirely underwater. The plane is inhabited by humanoid sea creatures, some of which resemble those we see in the real world. The preview video showed concept art of seals, sharks, and other marine life standing alongside merfolk and humans in full armor. As lead designer Mark Rosewater describes, the denizens of Nauctis fall into two categories: "humanoid" animals and "normal" animals. "The set has shark people, but it also has sharks," Rosewater says. "We have a lot of humanoid versions of things, but there's also just the normal versions of the animals in the world." However, not every being living in Nauctis is grounded in reality; "We are a fantasy game, we can make stuff up, and we did in fact make…

title: Nintendo’s Shigeru Miyamoto Defends Remakes Ahead Of Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Remake
description: Gaming legend Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of Mario and The Legend of Zelda, has spoken up to defend remakes. A lot of people embrace and enjoy remakes, while others say developers should instead spend more time and resources on entirely new games. Miyamoto, for his part, said remakes are good, actually, because a lot of people might have missed out on a game when it was originally released. Beyond that, commercial success of a remake can lead to additional resources that a company can use to put into new projects, Miyamoto said. “Some people might say there are a lot of remakes, but after five years, a lot of people have outgrown games and stop playing them. Young people today don’t have the opportunity to play games from 10 years ago, so remaking them to be more playable and releasing them again is a good way to meet the demand," he told Famitsu, as translated by Nintendo Everything. "Letting people know the original games also leads to future developments, so we’ve been actively pursuing that recently.” Nintendo has released numerous remakes over the years, so it's not surprising to hear Miyamoto say what he said. The next big remake from Nintendo is The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time remake, which comes to Switch 2 this year. Remakes are popular across the entire gaming industry. The next big remake is Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the 2001 game (minus competitive multiplayer), and it launches in early access on July 23. A study from 2025 found that nearly all gamers played a remake or remaster the previous year. Another report found that, in 2025, remakes and remasters reached more than 138 million downloads.

title: Here’s How To Play Halo: Campaign Evolved With Your Friends Across Xbox, PlayStation, And PC
description: With Halo: Campaign Evolved's early access period set to kick off on July 23, you may be wondering just how to enable cross-platform play so you and your fellow Spartans can kick grunt butt across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. Well, the process is actually super simple, so let us break it down for you right here. As outlined in a July 22 blog on the Halo Waypoint site, playing this Halo remake with your friends is easy. All you have to do is know their Gamertag or Username, search for and add it to your Xbox friends list--either on the Xbox site, from the Xbox Game Bar, or in the Xbox mobile app--then add them to your party from the "Cross-Platform Friends" list of the "Play Co-op" menu when they're online. And just like that, you're playing Halo: Campaign Evolved with your friends on a platform other than an Xbox. Weird times we're living in, but it really is that simple. It's worth noting that you don't get immediate access to Halo: Campaign Evolved's early access just by buying the game. As is customary with these sorts of things, you’ll need to preorder the $70 Premium Edition to get into the early access pool. If you have preordered the $50 Standard Edition, you can upgrade to the Premium Edition to gain early access, but that will run your wallet $20, bringing the total to the Premium Edition price. And if you got it via Xbox Game Pass, you can upgrade to the Premium Edition for $20. Preordering either version nets you the Foundry Armory Pack, which comes with legendary looks for Master Chief's iconic Mark V Mjolnir armor. Opting for the Premium Edition comes with some extra goodies, though, such as a digital artbook and short story, as well as the game manual and five additional Master Chief armor skins and six weapon skins. Halo: Campaign Evolved will launch on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S on July 28-- and it's a day-one release on Xbox Game Pass. Be sure to check out the release times so you can be ready for when the game officially…

title: Analyst Says Sony Killing Physical PS5 Games “Dooms” Brick-And-Mortar Stores
description: Sony's decision to kill physical PlayStation games in January 2028 has, understandably, gotten under the skin of just about everyone. And while Disgea's creator says the company should just stop making consoles altogether if there won't be any more physical games, an analyst is sounding the alarm on how Sony's decision could be the death knell for brick-and-mortar gaming stores in the future. Michael Pachter, managing director of strategic planning at the LA-based financial services firm Wedbush Securities, spoke to CNBC on July 21 about the possible ramifications of Sony's choice. He said that the company's decision could save Sony some money, but it ultimately feels anti-consumer. Pachter then emphasized just how important the used-gaming market is for all consumers. "Realistically, at least 1/3 of games have been sold historically as used, and the games that were sold used also provided currency to the gamer who traded them in as cash to pay for new games," he said. "Brick and mortar game retail is doomed." This is in stark contrast to what GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen said on July 17. As the top man of one of the largest gaming retailers in the world, Cohen expressed how " totally irrelevant " physical games are to the company's overall business. It is true that software sales only make up 12% of GameStop's revenue, with collectibles (like Pokemon cards) accounting for 41.8% and hardware and accessories totaling nearly 40%. Gaming sales, new or used, are an ever-shrinking portion of GameStop's business, and there is data backing up just how little physical PlayStation 5 game sales contribute to Sony's business. But the numbers haven't stopped hundreds of thousands of people from signing a petition urging Sony to change its mind and continue producing discs. The internet also had thoughts on Sony putting physical games in a coffin, with many lampooning how play apparently does have limits. (This is a riff on Sony's common slogan: "Play has no limits.")

title: PlayStation Plus Subscribers Have 9 Games To Finish Before August Ends
description: PlayStation Plus has gotten several new games throughout the month, but as expected, several of them are also set to leave the subscription service's Game Catalog for Extra- and Premium-tier subscribers. In total, there'll be nine games exiting PS Plus on August 18, so you've only got a few weeks left to check out a fun zombie apocalypse adventure, a JRPG with an elegant hand-drawn art style, and one anime-inspired game that knows exactly who its target market is. Here's the full list: PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving on August 18 Bomber Crew (PS4) Clash: Artifacts of Chaos (PS5, PS4) Dead Island 2 (PS5, PS4) Earth Defense Force 6 (PS5, PS4) Harold Halibut (PS5) Onee Chanbara Origin (PS4) Roki (PS5) Space Crew (PS4) Unicorn Overlord (PS5, PS4) Dead Island 2 is the highest-profile exit for next month, and if you haven't checked it out yet, then you've missed out on a fun sequel. Stuck in development hell for several years, it eventually released on PC and consoles in 2023. Surprisingly goofy, extremely violent, and full of a surprising amount of character buildcrafting, it's a fun experience that has a great balance of action and survival. The other game you'll want to check out is Harold Halibut, especially if you've been craving an old-school point-and-click adventure. Harold Halibut wears that influence on its sleeve, and it also looks incredible thanks to the years of work that went into crafting its unique characters and world. While those games won't be around for much longer, you can grab three games right now if you're subscribed to any tier of PlayStation Plus--Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, For the King 2, and CrossCode. For members of PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium, the Game Catalog has already expanded with five games this month, including Rise of the Ronin, Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora, and Dying Light. title: The Backyard Baseball Revival Is Solid In Every Way But One
description: Growing up in the '90s and early aughts, Backyard Baseball was the game of my generation. What was once found in cereal boxes as a free pack-in became a brand that decorated millennial childhoods across many sequels and different sports. I was so excited when it was announced that someone had gotten the gears turning on bringing the beloved but, until recently, hard-to-find series back to modern platforms. The revival has included re-listings of several of the original games, plus a brand-new entry for Backyard Baseball. It's that one that maybe had the most riding on it, and for the most part, it delivers. Let's start with what works. Backyard Baseball, not to be confused with Backyard Ball '97, the new name for the original game's re-release, is essentially a complete remake. It stays very faithful to that original game, offering the same colorful roster of kid athletes playing on the same neighborhood fields, spouting off many of the same whimsical one-liners mid-game, and chasing championships. It adds some new touches, like additional unlockable team logos and a customizable player option that didn't make it into the series for a few years back in the day, but overall, it's purposely just as millennials left the game, only with an updated aesthetic that ditches the 2D artwork for 3D characters and environments. Though I wasn't sure about the new 3D style when it was first revealed, it's grown on me, and I've come to like it now. It's extremely vibrant but also adheres to the general stylings of the past games, including things like UI elements that look just like they always did. It's not the first 3D game in the series I've enjoyed anyway; those two GameCube entries were awesome. The backyard is just as you left it, for the most part. In most every way, the new Backyard Baseball is a hit. The kids' personalities still shine brightly at every opportunity, be it their walk-up music (which has just been patched to offer the original tracks alongside the…

title: Xbox Brings Backwards Compatibility To PC, Starting With Four Classics
description: Backwards compatibility is finally coming to PC, with Xbox announcing the initiative with four original Xbox classics now available to download on your desktop or handheld PC of choice. Starting today, you'll be able to download and play Blinx: The Time Sweeper, Fuzion Frenzy, Conker: Live and Reloaded, and Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge on PC. If you own these games already, or are subscribed to Xbox Game Pass, you'll automatically see them in your library via the Xbox app, as well as the option to purchase them if you don't. Xbox says that this is just the start of its backwards-compatibility efforts on PC, with the program still in an early-release phase. The releases come with a variety of enhancements, including 4x resolution scaling, customizable graphics modes, fullscreen and windowed support, language settings, and more. In the future, Xbox says it plans to also introduce Achievements to this selection of games and those that release in the future. Backaward compatibilty on PC is supported on most Windows hardware, including the ROG Xbox Ally and Ally X. You'll need to meet the following hardware specifications if you plan to dive into Xbox's storied gaming history: Minimum GPU: Nvidia GTX 950 or AMD Radeon RX 550 or Intel UHD 770 or Intel Arc A310 CPU: Min 4 Cores Intel Core i3-8100 or AMD Ryzen 3 1200 or AMD Ryzen™ Z2 A Processor RAM: 8GB OS: Windows 11 Drivers and Versions: Latest Version as of January 2026 Recommended GPU: Radeon RX 68005 or Nvidia GTX 1070 Ti or Intel Arc A770 CPU: 6 cores and 12 threads Intel Core i5-10400 or AMD Ryzen 5 3600 or AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme DirectX Version: DirectX12 API, Hardware Feature Level 11 GPU VRAM: 8GB OS: Windows 11 Drivers and Versions: Latest Version as of January 2026 Following Sony's announcement that it will end physical disc production from 2028, reports have suggested that Xbox is preparing a disc-to-digital program as it plans to ship its next-generation console, Project Helix, without a disc drive

title: Hasbro’s The Legend Of Zelda Figures Have Been Revealed, And They Look Pretty Great
description: Hasbro and Nintendo are teaming up for The Legend of Zelda toys, and the first have now been revealed as part of the start of San Diego Comic-Con. These include Zelda, Link, and Ganondorf figures, based on their designs from The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. The Zelda and Link figures are six-inch scale figures with 20+ points of articulation. The Zelda figure includes a Decayed Master Sword and interchangeable sword grip hand. The Link figure, meanwhile, includes a Hylian shield, Master Sword, and interchangeable Zonai power hand. Both are $28, with preorders starting today, July 22, at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET. The Ganondorf figure ($43) is also inspired by Tears of the Kingdom. He stands 7.5 inches tall and also has 20+ points of articulation. The Ganondorf figure also comes with the Gloom Sword, scabbard, and interchangeable sword grip hand. Like the Link and Zelda figures, the Ganondorf figure goes on sale today. You can see the store pages for each figure through the links below. Ganondorf ($43) Link ($28) Zelda ($28) As for the game series, the next entry in the franchise is a new remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which is coming to Switch 2 this year. In addition to the Ocarina of Time remake, there is a live-action The Legend of Zelda movie coming in 2027 from Sony Pictures and Nintendo. Benjamin Evan Ainsworth plays Link, with Bo Bragason portraying Zelda. Wes Ball (The Maze Runner, Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes) is directing, and the film shot at the same locations in New Zealand where Peter Jackson’s The Lord of the Rings franchise also filmed.
